articles.title: Concentration‑dependent switching between ligand‑like and solvent‑like lipid regulation in a model ion channel
articles.abstract: Abstract Cell membranes are not only protective barriers but also active chemical environments that regulate protein structure and function. However, how individual lipid species influence membrane proteins across physiological concentration ranges, either as specific ligands or through bilayer-mediated solvent effects, remains poorly defined. Here, using the cyclic nucleotide-gated ion channel SthK reconstituted into defined membranes, we show that phosphatidic acid enhances channel activity across all tested concentrations but, at low mole fractions ( ~ 0.7-1 mol%), it selectively and cooperatively increases agonist potency, meeting criteria for a site‑specific allosteric ligand. In contrast, the zwitterionic lipid phosphatidylethanolamine modulates SthK activity exclusively through linear, solvent‑like effects across the same concentration range. Structural analysis reveals that low anionic lipid content expands the closed‑state conformational ensemble without promoting pore opening, providing a structural basis for lipid-dependent latent allostery. Together, these results establish lipid concentration as a governing regulatory variable that quantitatively distinguishes ligand‑like from solvent‑like mechanisms of membrane protein regulation.

articles.title: High-content morphological profiling by Cell Painting in 3D spheroids
articles.abstract: Abstract Cell Painting is a popular high-content imaging assay that captures the shape and internal organization of 2D cell cultures at scale. While 3D cell cultures are more physiologically relevant models – especially for studying drug perturbations – they remain challenging to image because light scatters before it reaches the cultures’ interior. Here, we introduce a scalable method to adapt Cell Painting for 3D spheroids. We show that tissue-clearing, a technique that makes spheroids transparent, combined with a focusing routine that locates spheroids on the fly, enables Cell Painting at single-cell level inside intact spheroids. By profiling 52 clinically relevant drugs, we show that single-cell fingerprints clustered by biological pathway and resolved drug effects more robustly than those of flattened spheroid-wide views. Notably, the effect of two drugs, 5-fluorouracil and olaparib, nearly indistinguishable in 2D monolayers, diverged in spheroids. This finding was then corroborated by DNA-damage, cell-cycle, and gene-expression assays. The workflow runs on a spinning-disk confocal microscope in a standard 384-well plate format, making single-cell 3D profiling accessible to laboratories already performing Cell Painting.

articles.title: Orbital coupling effect enables low-chloride concentration electrolyte for four-electron redox in aqueous zinc | |iodine batteries
Kinetic acceleration of phosphate remediation in dilute aquatic environments via photovoltaic-driven solid-state electrolyte electrocoagulation
Strain-engineered fabrication of high-density aligned graphene-based nanoscrolls via UV-tunable adhesive tapes
articles.abstract: Abstract Graphene nanoscrolls (GNSs), one-dimensional nanostructures formed by rolling up a single sheet of graphene, exhibit electronic and mechanical properties distinct from the original graphene sheet. Although several methods have been proposed to synthesize GNSs, achieving high-density GNSs with controlled scroll chirality and direction remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate the strain-engineered fabrication of large-scale GNSs using an ultraviolet (UV) light-tunable adhesive tape. The UV tape is stretched to apply tensile strain to graphene stacked on it, and releasing the applied strain by detaching the graphene from the tape results in the formation of GNSs. This strain-assisted method gives isolated GNSs of increased density ( ≈ 380 nanoscrolls per mm) and length (90 μm). This method also allows control of the scroll angle, i.e., chiral angle, by controlling the stretch direction of the tape/graphene stack. The nanoscroll structure allows the intercalation of metal chloride molecules, resulting in an increase of the electrical conductivity. Furthermore, heteronanoscrolls of graphene and MoS 2 are realized by stretching MoS 2 /graphene heterostacks, exhibiting clear optical response. Our controlled synthesis of GNSs and heteronanoscrolls provides an opportunity to manipulate nanomaterials through the strain engineering with the functional UV tape.

articles.title: HRDPath: an explainable multi-model deep learning architecture for predicting homologous recombination deficiency from histopathology images
articles.abstract: Abstract Homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) is a critical biomarker for guiding treatment decisions in high-grade serous tubo-ovarian carcinoma (HGSOC), a cancer with few reliable biomarkers. However, existing genomics-based tests for HRD are variable, expensive, and time-consuming. We develop HRDPath, a patient-level deep learning architecture that predicts HRD status from whole slide images, requiring no additional molecular testing. HRDPath is validated across three cohorts of female patients and achieves an AUC of 0.846, significantly outperforming previously reported results in HGSOC. By incorporating multiple slides per patient and targeted optimization strategies, we strengthen the model clinical utility, with both specificity and sensitivity reaching 0.90. Our interpretability pipeline enhances model trustworthiness and reveals important clinical and biological insights into HRD-positive cancers, highlighting the associated morphological and pathological changes at the cellular and tissue levels. HRDPath provides a foundation for an accessible and scalable digital biomarker to improve treatment stratification in ovarian cancer globally.

articles.title: Longitudinal ctDNA profiling reveals genomic risk and molecular response to bireociclib in advanced breast cancer
Preferred evolutionary routes of convergence in Klebsiella pneumoniae favor siderophore acquisition over hypervirulence
articles.abstract: Abstract The rise of Klebsiella pneumoniae combining antimicrobial resistance and virulence genes poses a major health threat, but the evolutionary routes and phenotypic consequences of this convergence are poorly understood. Here, phylogenetics of 1468 isolates and population analysis of 7520 plasmids, from >50 countries through the last two decades, reveal that convergence follows preferred, constrained evolutionary paths. The dominant route involves multidrug-resistant classical K. pneumoniae acquiring conjugative IncFIB(Mar)/IncHI1B(Mar) plasmids carrying an incomplete set of virulence biomarkers. Across 25 independent convergence events, the acquisition of the aerobactin siderophore locus was the only universal feature. These convergent isolates exhibit enhanced siderophore production but consistently lack the hypervirulent phenotype in vivo. In contrast, genuine hypervirulent strains that gain resistance remain rare. We conclude that enhanced siderophore production, not hypervirulence, is the primary adaptive trait driving the success of globally emerging convergent lineages, representing a distinct evolutionary state optimized for transmission rather than systemic invasion.

articles.title: Controlled living ring expansion polymerization for the precision synthesis of cyclic poly(aryl isocyanides)
Ethnoracial disparities in emergency department triage are more pronounced in lower-risk visits: a multicenter study
Spatiotemporal analysis of insecticide-treated bednet coverage, age and type in Africa from 2006-2024
articles.abstract: Abstract Since their rapid adoption from the mid 2000s, insecticide-treated nets (ITNs) have been one of the most impactful malaria interventions in Africa. Facing insecticide resistance and ever-increasing resource constraints, there is a growing need to revise previous modelling efforts of ITN coverage to better reflect the current epidemiological reality. Comprehensive estimates of ITN coverage must account for factors such as net type, net age, and user behaviours. By leveraging improved data availability, we propose a mathematically rigorous ITN coverage model that extends previous national-level models to the subnational level across 44 countries in Africa. The presented Multitype-ITN (MITN) model is used to construct longitudinal estimates of net demography by age and type from 2006-2024, and provide insights on potential sources of ITN distribution inefficiencies. Our findings show a significant increase in the uptake of next-generation ITNs, reflecting an increasingly diverse market. However, longitudinal trends suggests stagnation in key metrics of net coverage (nets-per-capita, access and use), alongside a downwards trend in utilisation – number of users per net, coupled with observed stationary use rates – proportion of people with access that also use nets. There are also early signs of interventions failing to meet the demands of increasing populations.

articles.title: Silk fibroin intrinsically activates Ccl27⁺ migratory-paracrine keratinocytes to orchestrate epidermal–dermal crosstalk for regenerative wound healing
Engineering the paclitaxel biosynthetic pathway in Physcomitrium patens for de novo and stable biosynthesis
articles.abstract: Abstract Paclitaxel is a highly valuable diterpenoid anticancer drug originally extracted from the yew tree. Due to the low efficiency of plant extraction and the high cost of semi-synthesis, efforts have been made to produce paclitaxel through biosynthesis. However, there have been no reports to date on engineered strains capable of paclitaxel biosynthesis. Here, we engineer a paclitaxel-producing line using the moss ( Physcomitrium patens ) chassis cells by combining transient expression verification, cytoplasmic localization strategies, self-cleaving 2 A peptide-mediated multi-gene co-expression systems and a modular iterative transformation strategy for stable genetic inheritance. Even after continuous subculturing multiple times, the engineered paclitaxel-producing lines obtained through both the initial reconstructed pathway and the optimized pathway are able to stably produce paclitaxel. This study proposes that Physcomitrium patens can serve as a plant chassis for paclitaxel biosynthesis.

articles.title: Sevuparin in children with severe malaria: a phase I safety and dose-finding trial
articles.abstract: Abstract Mortality rates for African children with severe malaria remain high. Sevuparin, a heparin-like compound, as an adjunctive treatment, may improve outcomes due to its effects on Plasmodium falciparum -infected erythrocytes. A Phase I dose-finding trial in Kenyan and Zambian children with severe malaria aimed to identify the maximum tolerated dose (MTD) of sevuparin, given as three infusions (at 0, 8 and 16 h post-enrolment) using the continual reassessment method (ISRCTN32271864). The primary endpoint was dose limiting toxicity (DLT) defined as Activated Partial Thromboplastin Time (APTT) > 95 seconds (2.5x upper limit of normal) across 1.5-6 mg/kg doses. Secondary endpoints were lactate clearance, parasite half-life, APTT at 24 h and grade 3-4 serious adverse events. Twenty-three children were enroled; 20 were included in the primary analysis, across 10 cohorts. A data monitoring committee followed model recommendations, leading to dose escalation from 1.5 mg/kg through all doses to 6 mg/kg when 2 DLTs occurred. During de-escalation, DLTs occurred at 5 mg/kg and 4 mg/kg. The final dose was therefore 3 mg/kg. There was 1 death (1/23 (4.3%)), 1 readmission and 1 grade 3 non-DLT adverse event: all judged unrelated to sevuparin. MTD of 3 mg/kg sevuparin in each of three infusions at 0, 8 and 16 h was identified for future investigation.

articles.title: Tumor-intrinsic PTPN12 suppresses anti-tumor immunity in colorectal cancer by restraining a dual epigenetic and cytoskeletal dsRNA sensing program
PRMT5 activity sustains histone production to maintain genome integrity
articles.abstract: Abstract Histone proteins package DNA into nucleosomes, forming chromatin and thereby safeguarding genome integrity. Proper histone expression is essential for cell proliferation and chromatin organization, yet the upstream regulators of histone supply remain incompletely understood. PRMT5, a protein arginine methyltransferase that catalyzes symmetric dimethylation of arginine residues, is frequently overexpressed in cancer and targeted in multiple clinical trials, but its cell-essential function remains unclear. Using time-resolved nascent transcriptional profiling, quantitative proteomics, and imaging, we show that PRMT5 activity is required to sustain histone transcription and histone protein synthesis during S phase. PRMT5 inhibition or knockdown leads to rapid, p53-independent depletion of histone mRNA, leading to loss of histone proteins and accumulation of replication-associated nuclear abnormalities. Parallel depletion of the histone gene transcription factor HINFP produces similar genomic instability, linking defective histone production to loss of genome integrity. We further show that histone H4 accumulates at both histone genes and histone locus bodies (HLBs) and that H4R3me2s is enriched at HLBs. These findings support a model in which PRMT5-mediated methylation of histone H4 regulates histone transcription. Our findings establish PRMT5 as a central coordinator of histone homeostasis and provide a mechanistic rationale for its essential role in proliferating cells.

articles.title: A dynamically tunable diamine ligand enables Cu-catalyzed enantioselective nucleophilic substitution at P(V)
Thermal sculpting of nanoconfined single-atom cavities enables urea electrosynthesis with near-unity selectivity
articles.abstract: Abstract Electrocatalytic urea synthesis from CO 2 and NO 3 – offers a sustainable alternative to energy-intensive industrial methods, yet precise C–N coupling remains hindered by kinetic mismatches between the reduction reactions. Here, we report a strategy leveraging programmable Zn-node gasification to thermally sculpt 1.5–1.8 nm cavities within zeolitic imidazolate frameworks, hosting atomically dispersed Cu–N 4 sites. Thermal transformation creates size-matched nanoconfined environments for selective catalysis. An optimal confinement metric descriptor (9.64) is introduced as a predictive parameter, correlating cavity geometry with local electric-field and Cu d-band modulation. This design stabilizes *CO and *NO intermediates, effectively suppressing parasitic reactions and lowering C–N coupling barriers. Consequently, the catalyst delivers a urea yield of 71.32 g g cat –1 h –1 with 98.9% Faradaic efficiency (FE) in gas diffusion cells. Pilot-scale testing demonstrates stable operation over 300 h with an FE of 90%, establishing nanoconfinement as a design principle for competitive-performance urea electrosynthesis.

articles.title:
Establishing
an
Air Health Index for Predicting the
Risk of Acute Myocardial Infarction Onset Associated with Air Pollution
and Ambient Temperature
articles.abstract: Abstract Air pollutants and ambient temperature are important cardiovascular disease determinants, and communicating their overall risk is important for cardiovascular patient management. We developed a composite Air Health Index (AHI) by linking high-resolution exposure data with 1,207,625 acute myocardial infarction (AMI) cases across 325 Chinese cities. The AHI for AMI aggregates excess morbidity risks from fine particulate matter, nitrogen dioxide, ozone, and ambient temperature into a normalized scale (0–10+). Compared with existing metrics, the AHI for AMI showed better predictive performance for AMI onset than the Air Quality Index (AQI) and Air Quality Health Index (AQHI). Each interquartile range increase in the AHI for AMI was associated with a 5.97% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 5.32%–6.63%) increase in AMI incidence, surpassing the AQHI (3.33%, 95% CI: 2.93%–3.72%) and AQI (2.04%, 95% CI: 1.73%–2.35%). The AHI for AMI showed a nearly linear exposure–response relationship with no evident threshold and accounted for 8,534 per 100,000 AMI cases nationally. These associations were consistently validated in an independent external data set, supporting the robustness and generalizability of the index. In conclusion, the AHI for AMI provides an integrative and practical framework for assessing environmental health risks, offering actionable guidance for cardiovascular patient management.

articles.title:
The New Frontiers
in Endocrine Disruption Research
and Policy
articles.abstract: Abstract Since the 1991 Wingspread Consensus Statement, the field of endocrine disruption has emerged as a distinct and complex area that continues to challenge conventional approaches to toxicology and risk assessment. Nonetheless, despite substantial scientific advances, including the identification of over 1,000 Endocrine Disrupting Chemicals (EDCs), the description of nonmonotonic dose–response relationships, and the elucidation of multiple mechanisms of action, regulatory progress continues to lag. Recent stagnation in research investment into EDCs reflects a persistent tension between robust scientific evidence and policy implementation for environmental chemicals, which is especially salient for those bearing the unique properties and concerns of endocrine disruptors. In this article, we delineate the lull in EDC research that began in the mid-to-late 2010s and discuss how per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) have refocused public, scientific, and regulatory attention away from EDCs. While PFAS qualify as EDCs, their structural similarity and environmental persistence enable regulatory pathways that circumvent traditional research bottlenecks confronting other endocrine disruptors. This divergence presents both opportunities and potential drawbacks: while PFAS regulation may revitalize the broader EDC field, overemphasis on PFAS could perpetuate longstanding challenges in chemical prioritization, mixture assessment, and cumulative risk evaluation. We highlight state-level initiatives in Maine, Minnesota, and Washington as promising models for adaptive regulation. Moving forward, coordinated action among states, industry, academia, and civil society will be essential to advancing protective EDC policy while maintaining scientific rigor and feasibility.

articles.title:
Atmospheric
Observations
Reveal the Spatial Influence
of Inland Shipping Channels and Enhanced Emission Signals from AIS-Unmatched
Vessels
articles.abstract: Abstract Inland shipping is an important but poorly constrained source of urban air pollution, particularly in dense waterway networks, where vessel activity records are incomplete. Here, we integrate high-time-resolution differential optical absorption spectroscopy (DOAS), national air-quality observations, meteorological normalization, spatial exposure analysis, automatic identification system (AIS) records, and field photographs to evaluate inland shipping impacts in two representative channel environments in eastern China. SO2 showed stronger spatial heterogeneity than nitrogen-related pollutants and was more closely associated with the nearby shipping channels. After meteorological normalization, inland-waterway configuration explained 44% of the interstation variability in urban SO2, with the strongest association at an influence distance of approximately 4 km. Event-scale analysis revealed frequent short-term pollutant enhancements associated with the vessel passages. However, only 54.4% of plume events at the open-channel station and 44.8% at the lock-controlled site could be matched to AIS-recorded vessels. AIS-unmatched plume events were not negligible and, in the lock-controlled environment, were associated with SO2 signals higher than those of AIS-matched events. These results demonstrate that atmospheric observations provide an independent constraint on underdetected inland shipping emissions and suggest that inventories relying solely on vessel activity records may underestimate or mischaracterize sulfur-related emissions from inland waterways.

articles.title:
The Fate of Per-
and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS)
in Municipal Solid Waste Incineration: Atmospheric Emissions from
a Waste-to-Energy Plant
articles.abstract: Abstract The atmospheric fate of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) represents a very recent field of research. While ISO and CEN standards are yet under development, PFAS have been identified during the past years in atmospheric emissions, ambient air, and deposition. As high-quality field data are currently scarce, the objectives of this study were to (i) characterize atmospheric PFAS emissions of a state-of-the-art waste-to-energy (WtE) plant under representative operational conditions and (ii) evaluate the emission impact in ambient air in the vicinity of the plant. Results suggest a contribution from the WtE plant at the nearest ambient monitoring location, 450 m downwind of the plant, with a measurable contribution and distinct PFAS fingerprint closely matching the emission profiles independently characterized at two grate incinerator lines. Quantified PFAS emissions do not exceed the temporary assessment framework for ambient air in Flanders. Furthermore, optimization of the activated carbon (AC) dosage achieved a 95% reduction in emissions at line 1, with subsequent emission levels approaching those of field blanks. The waste treatment sector represents a critical frontier of environmental management. Building experimental evidence of potential PFAS releases will be key to ensure comprehensive strategies for responsible PFAS management in the years ahead.

articles.title:
Nanozyme-Based
Analytical
Platforms for Environmental
Pollutants: Classification, Catalytic Mechanisms, and Multimodal Strategies
articles.abstract: Abstract The precise trace pollutant analysis within complex environmental matrices demands robust, highly specific, and anti-interference analytical platforms. Nanozymes, possessing tunable enzyme-like catalytic activities, superior thermodynamic stability, and cost effectiveness, have emerged as innovative tools in environmental analytical chemistry. This Review systematically discusses the integration of diverse nanozymes (metal, metal oxide, carbon, hybrid-structured, and multimetallic alloy) across foundational analytical methodologies, including colorimetric, fluorometric, electrochemical, chemiluminescence, and surface-enhanced Raman scattering assays. To overcome the matrix interference present in real-world samples, this Review highlights the pivotal evolution from conventional single-signal detection to advanced multimodal sensing approaches. The incorporation of molecular imprinting, microfluidics, and photothermal technologies effectively mitigates matrix interference, enhances mass transfer, and eliminates false positives through multidimensional cross-validation. Furthermore, atomic-level regulation strategies including defect engineering, asymmetric coordination, and high-entropy synergistic effects are presented to address inherent limitations such as catalytic passivation and nanoparticle aggregation. A unified standardization metric framework is also proposed for rigorous analytical performance evaluation. Finally, a perspective is provided on coupling artificial intelligence and machine learning with the nanozyme-based sensing platform, guiding a pathway from empirical trial-and-error to the rational and data-driven design of next-generation intelligent environmental analytical systems.

articles.title: The Emirati pangenome featuring a diploid chromosome-level reference
Nutrient stress-driven ACSS1 controls metabolic flexibility and bone formation

60 Years of Biogeochemistry
and Remediation Science

Resource-Oriented
Wastewater Treatment through Quorum
Quenching─Integration of AnMBR and Donnan Dialysis
articles.abstract: Abstract Aligned with United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 6, water treatment is shifting from pollution removal to resource recovery and circularity. An integration of AnMBR and a Donnan dialysis (DD) (AnMBR-DD) was proposed to simultaneously recover methane and ammonium, and quorum quenching (QQ) was further incorporated to mitigate membrane fouling and enhance process efficiency. The COD removal efficiency was stably maintained above 80%, and the methane conversion efficiency reached 51.6%. The effluent NH4+-N concentration was controlled at 3–5 mg/L, with a recovery efficiency of 47.1% in the AnMBR-DD. The QQ effectively alleviated biofouling on the ultrafiltration membrane in the AnMBR and ion exchange membrane in the DD, while improving methane production and ammonia recovery by 20.6% and 6.6%, respectively. These improvements were mainly attributed to QQ-induced reductions in extracellular polymeric substances (EPS), which weakened microbial adhesion and decreased biofilm compactness. Life cycle assessment showed that coupled methane and ammonium recovery in AnMBR-DD-QQ were the decided advantages in alleviating the environmental impact. These results highlight the great potential of AnMBR-DD-QQ as a resource-oriented wastewater treatment strategy.

articles.title:
Molecular
Evolution of Dissolved Organic Nitrogen
from Photoaged Nitrogen-Containing Microplastics Reveals Amine Structures
as Key Nitrosamine Precursors
articles.abstract: Abstract Although dissolved organic nitrogen (DON) is continuously released and transformed as nitrogen-containing microplastics (N-MPs) age, the evolution of this replenished pool and its reactivity during downstream chloramination remains unresolved. Here, we tracked the compositional evolution of DON molecules in polyamide (PA) and polyacrylonitrile (PAN) suspensions under UV irradiation using a nitrogen atom-based molecular classification strategy (N1–N5). After 7 d of irradiation-induced molecular reorganization, N1–N5 molecules accounted for 87% and 79% of the molecular signal intensity in PA-DOM and PAN-DOM, respectively. Eight annotated compounds followed increasing, decreasing, or transient accumulation trajectories, revealing simultaneous molecular accumulation and depletion. Reaction-network analysis further showed that N1–N5 molecules progressively became the dominant reactants, and these trajectories were dominated by oxidation and accompanied by increasingly frequent amine-related transformation links. Structural analysis revealed amide-rich N1–N2 and N-heterocycle-rich N3–N5 molecules, while secondary and tertiary amines occurred across all N1–N5 classes. As this molecular reorganization progressed, N-MP-DON level dropped, but substantially enhanced N-nitrosodimethylamine and N-nitrosodiethylamine formation, and potential precursor identification was strongly associated with amine structures, rather than nitrogen atom number. Overall, our study highlights N-MP-DON as a potential source of nitrosamine precursors, and the need to carefully consider amine-containing additives use in plastic manufacturing.

articles.title: Issue Publication Information

Toward a Universal
Switch for Microbial Granulation:
Photogranule Insights to Advance Granular Wastewater Treatment
articles.abstract: Abstract Microbial granulation─the assembly of self-immobilized, spheroidal aggregates─is a transformative approach for high-density, energy-efficient wastewater treatment. By concentrating biomass and enhancing resilience to influent fluctuations, granular systems significantly reduce infrastructure footprints. Current granular technologies primarily leverage upflow continuous reactors or sequencing-batch reactors, where specific external selection pressures are imposed to drive granulation. However, granulation remains neither spontaneous nor reliably predictable, and its fundamental biological drivers are poorly understood. Recent advances in photogranules challenge selection-pressure models. Photogranules form from activated-sludge inocula in hydrostatic and hydrodynamic batches and even in CSTRs where classical selection conditions are weak or absent. Moreover, the recurring emergence of compact spheroidal granules across diverse natural and laboratory systems suggests shared, intrinsic biological drivers rather than purely engineered causes. In this Perspective, we propose that the bacterial second messenger c-di-GMP functions as a conserved, Goldilocks-like molecular switch that integrates diverse environmental cues into a coordinated granulation program. We synthesize transcriptomic, biochemical, and genetic evidence and advance three hypotheses linking c-di-GMP signaling and community physiology to granulation. If validated, targeted modulation of c-di-GMP─by genetic or chemical means─could enable predictable, resilient granulation across a wider range of systems, including the continuous horizontal-flow basins that dominate wastewater infrastructure.

articles.title:
Enantiomer-Dependent
Modulation of Lithium Uptake
and Accumulation in Plants by Foliar Application of Chiral SeNPs
articles.abstract: Abstract The rapid expansion of lithium-based new energy technologies has led to substantial lithium inputs into soil, potentially threatening human health through the consumption of lithium-accumulated agricultural products. Therefore, efficient strategies are urgently needed to mitigate the uptake and accumulation of lithium in plant fruits. Nanotechnology offers promising avenues for enhancing stress resilience and improving the quality of crops grown in contaminated soils. Here, we found that lithium was distributed unevenly among tissues (leaves: 1365, roots: 508, stems: 112, and fruits: 24 mg kg–1) of eggplants grown in lithium-contaminated soil. Notably, foliar spraying of selenium nanoparticles with levorotatory chirality (l-SeNPs) effectively reduced fruit lithium content and promoted its accumulation in the leaves, roots, and stems, in which vacuolar compartmentalization was the primary pathway for tolerance to high lithium content, whereas the dextrorotatory enantiomer showed no such effects. Mechanism investigation elucidated that l-SeNPs can reinforce antioxidant defense systems of eggplant under lithium stress through a microbiome–metabolome–transcriptome bridging cascade, in which l-SeNPs substantially affected rhizosphere bacterial and metabolic networks along with minor changes in the bioavailability of lithium in rhizosphere soil. This study sheds light on the superiority of nanoscale chirality in modulating lithium uptake and accumulation in plants grown in metal-contaminated soil, providing strategies for agromining of lithium.

articles.title:
Depth-Independent
Soil Organic Carbon Persistence
across Climate Gradients in Coastal Wetlands
articles.abstract: Abstract Coastal wetland soils constitute a major global blue carbon pool. Yet, how soil organic carbon (SOC) persistence varies with soil depth and responds to climate change remains poorly understood. Here, we assessed depth-related patterns and climatic controls on SOC persistence using radiocarbon (Δ14C) measurements from 82 samples across 41 sites spanning temperate to tropical coastal wetlands. Radiocarbon-inferred SOC persistence did not differ significantly between topsoil (0–10 cm) and subsoil (40–60 cm) across climate zones and wetland types, with mean Δ14C values of −179.0 ± 155.5‰ and −200.9 ± 161.8‰, respectively (p > 0.05). Interactions among climate, vegetation, and soil biogeochemistry explained about 55% of the variation in SOC persistence in both topsoil and subsoil. Both layers exhibited comparable sensitivity to mean annual temperature and precipitation. However, the inferred regulatory pathways differed between soil layers, with stronger direct climatic effects in topsoil and greater indirect mediation through soil physicochemical and mineral-associated processes in subsoil. Across spatial climatic gradients, higher mean annual temperature and precipitation were associated with greater SOC accumulation but lower persistence, suggesting a potential trade-off between SOC quantity and persistence. These findings demonstrate limited vertical differentiation in SOC persistence between the 0–10 cm and 40–60 cm layers and highlight the need to better represent depth-specific regulatory processes in carbon-climate feedback frameworks.

articles.title: Issue Editorial Masthead
A Multidimensional Framework for Integrated Toxicity Assessment and Prioritization of Naphthenic Acids in Marine Medaka ( Oryzias melastigma ): Neurotoxicity and Mechanistic Insights
articles.abstract: Abstract Petroleum pollution poses a major challenge to global environmental health. Petroleum-derived naphthenic acids (NAs) are frequently detected in marine environments, yet their multidimensional toxicity and mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we developed an integrated toxicity framework combining bioassays, toxicity screening, computational simulations, transcriptomics, and bioinformatics to characterize NAs toxicity in marine medaka (Oryzias melastigma). A concentration gradient spanning environmentally detected levels to higher-effect concentrations (0.015–30 mg/L) revealed developmental defects, cardiac suppression, behavioral disruption, and metabolic dysfunction. CRITIC–AHP-based prioritization identified neurotoxicity as the predominant toxicity dimension, with cyclopentylpropionic acid (CPPA) and cyclohexylpropionic acid (CHPA) identified as major contributors. Mechanistically, these compounds were associated with distinct candidate pathways involving CXCR3-CXCL10 neuroinflammatory responses and DPP10-Kv4.2 ion homeostasis disruption. Their divergent toxicity profiles may be associated with differences in hydrophobicity and molecular flexibility. Rescue experiments supported these pathways, restoring swimming velocity by 60.32% and 62.09%, respectively. Furthermore, NAs induced neurobehavioral alterations and transcriptional signatures overlapping with Alzheimer’s disease-associated genes, with 14 and 12 candidate genes identified for CPPA and CHPA. Collectively, this study provides a cross-scale perspective linking physicochemical properties, toxicity pathways, and adverse outcomes of NAs, offering a conceptual approach for toxicity screening and mechanism elucidation of contaminants.

articles.title:
Heterogeneous
Component
Degradation Controls Molecular
Evolution and Reactivity of Volatile Organic Compounds during Distiller’s
Grains Pyrolysis
articles.abstract: Abstract Biomass pyrolysis is a crucial method of resource utilization, but resulting volatiles may pose environmental concerns due to their impacts on air quality and secondary pollution. However, the mechanisms governing thermal degradation and volatile evolution remain unclear. Herein, we integrate online thermogravimetry–Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy–gas chromatography/mass spectrometry, Gaussian deconvolution, and two-dimensional correlation spectroscopy to elucidate the degradation characteristics and sequential temperature-dependent volatile evolution of distiller’s grains (DG), a protein-rich agro-industrial residue. DG pyrolysis exhibited distinct multistage degradation characteristics governed by coupled decomposition and synergistic interactions of lignocellulosic and protein-derived components. The major volatiles included alcohols/ethers, phenols/esters, hydrocarbons, and aromatics, with pronounced temperature-dependent variations. Volatile and intermediate-volatility organic compounds accounted for 47–60% and 35–52% of total detected organic volatile emissions released during pyrolysis, respectively. Most DG-derived volatiles exhibited reducing characteristics, with average carbon oxidation states below zero, while broad saturation mass concentration distributions reflected substantial chemical heterogeneity. The temperature-dependent evolution sequence of DG-derived volatiles followed alcohols/phenols → aromatics/hydrocarbons → aldehydes/ketones/acids → esters → CO2/CH4/NH3. A DG mechanistic framework was proposed, demonstrating that heterogeneous component degradation regulated dynamic volatile generation and variation. These findings provide mechanistic insight into DG pyrolysis and contribute to sustainable biomass valorization and environmental impact assessment.

articles.title:
Warming Patterns
Shape Divergent Multilevel Physiological
Responses and Underlying Metabolic Mechanisms in Aquatic Organisms
articles.abstract: Abstract Although the impacts of global warming on aquatic ecosystems are widely recognized, the biological consequences of distinct warming patterns remain largely unknown. We investigated physiological and metabolic responses of Daphnia magna, Chironomus kiiensis, and zebrafish under constant warming (+1, +3 °C), heatwave, and temperature fluctuation. Dynamic patterns exhibited stronger physiological responses, with mean absolute effect sizes across survival, growth, development, behavior, and stress functional categories following the order heatwave > fluctuation > +3 °C > +1 °C. Response profiles varied among warming patterns: constant +3 °C induced moderate and broad changes across biochemical stress, developmental, and behavioral end points; heatwave accelerated zebrafish hatching and C. kiiensis pupation while increasing deformity, suppressing growth, and elevating mortality; and fluctuation induced pronounced biochemical stress responses, particularly HSP70, together with developmental disruption, while producing weaker survival and growth effects than heatwave. Across taxa, dominant response profiles differed, with broad multiend point disruption in D. magna, stress-dominant responses in C. kiiensis, and developmental sensitivity in zebrafish. Metabolomic analysis further identified warming-pattern-specific metabolic signatures associated with energy metabolism under +3 °C, membrane-related processes under heatwave, and redox-related processes under fluctuation. Together, these findings provide a scientific basis for improving aquatic ecological risk assessment under increasingly variable warming scenarios.

articles.title:
Landscape
Fire-Sourced PM2.5 and Cause-Specific
Renal Hospitalizations: A Multicountry Two-Stage Time-Series Analysis
of 12.5 Million Admissions
articles.abstract: Abstract Landscape fire-sourced PM2.5 (LFS PM2.5) is increasingly recognized as an important air pollutant, but its short-term contribution to renal hospitalizations remains unclear. Here, we assessed the associations between LFS PM2.5 and renal hospitalizations across 1020 locations in Australia, Brazil, Canada, Chile, New Zealand, and Thailand during 2000–2019 using a two-stage time-series design and estimated the attributable hospitalizations. LFS PM2.5 was associated with increased renal hospitalization risk, with the strongest associations observed for acute kidney injury. A 10 μg/m3 increase in cumulative LFS PM2.5 exposure over lag 0–5 was associated with a 1.1% increase in renal hospitalizations (RR = 1.011, 95% CI: 1.007–1.015). Associations were stronger in warmer areas and differed across levels of GDP per capita. Associations were consistently stronger for LFS PM2.5 than for non-LFS PM2.5. We estimated that LFS PM2.5 contributed to 1.38 renal hospitalizations per 100,000 population annually across the study regions. These findings highlight renal disease as an underrecognized health consequence of landscape fire smoke and support strengthened strategies to reduce wildfire smoke exposure under a changing climate.

articles.title:
Psychoactive
Pollutant
Impacts Baseline Immune Traits
but Not Behavior and Microbiome in a Fish
articles.abstract: Abstract Pharmaceutical pollution is an increasing global threat to freshwater ecosystems. Psychoactive drugs, such as antidepressants, are of particular concern because they affect evolutionarily conserved neuroendocrine pathways in nontarget organisms. As these pathways regulate interconnected biological systems, understanding the ecological consequences of pharmaceutical exposure requires an integrative approach. Here, we investigated the effects of 28-day exposure to control (freshwater), low (4.2 ± 0.3 ng/L), and high (637.5 ± 173.84 ng/L) fluoxetine concentrations on behaviors, baseline immune traits, and skin mucus microbiome composition in the Murray River rainbowfish (Melanotaenia fluviatilis). Fluoxetine exposure did not impact fish behavior, including activity, freezing behavior, shelter use, or microbiome composition. In contrast, immune traits were significantly altered. Both fluoxetine concentrations reduced total white blood cell (WBC) count, while only fish exposed to the low concentration showed reduced lymphocyte counts and elevated neutrophil counts, consistent with a stress-associated WBC redistribution response. Our findings show that different, but interconnected, biological systems can differ in their sensitivity to pollutants and suggest that immune traits may be an early, sensitive indicator of exposure to psychoactive pharmaceuticals. These findings highlight the importance of integrating multiple biological end points to obtain a more comprehensive understanding of the ecological consequences of pharmaceutical contamination.

articles.title:
Dual
Oxidation in the Amino Acid-Mediated Copper-Catalyzed
Fenton-like System: Effects of Ligand Structure and pH-Dependent Speciation
articles.abstract: Abstract The Cu(II)/H2O2 system has attracted increasing interest as a Cu-catalyzed advanced oxidation process and serves as a useful biomimetic model for investigating Cu-mediated biomolecule redox interactions. In this system, reactive oxidants can operate in a dual-oxidation mode, where the oxidant flux partitions between coordinated ligands and coexisting bulk-phase substrates. In this study, we systematically investigated this behavior over a wide pH range (3–12), using 17 structurally diverse amino acids (AAs) as model ligands and benzoic acid (BA), which exhibits negligible Cu(II) complexation, as a model bulk-phase substrate. Speciation-based kinetic analysis identified the bis-chelated complex, [Cu(AA)2], as a key catalytic species associated with effective dual oxidation, namely, balanced oxidant allocation between ligand-centered AA oxidation and bulk-phase BA oxidation, at pH 7–10. Using quantitative structure–activity/efficiency relationships, we demonstrate that the partitioning of oxidant flux is governed by two ligand-associated properties: (i) Cu(II)-binding strength, which promotes ligand-centered oxidation, and (ii) oxidative stability (proxied by the highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO)–lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO) gap), which favors the oxidant flux to the bulk phase. At higher pH, the possible formation of mixed hydroxo species, [Cu(AA)2(OH)]−, was associated with a shift toward ligand-centered oxidation and attenuated bulk-phase BA oxidation. Integrated machine-learning models combining ligand descriptors with pH-dependent speciation indicators further supported these trends and predicted AA and BA oxidation kinetics across pH 7–11. These results provide a predictive framework for understanding how ligand structure and pH-dependent speciation jointly control oxidant allocation in the Cu(II)/H2O2 system.
